blurb: The characters Japanese children meet first — numbers, days of the week, up and down, people and nature.
sample: 一右雨円王音下火花貝学気

blurb: Everyday words start forming: seasons, family, coming and going, thinking and speaking.
sample: 引羽雲園遠何科夏家歌画回

blurb: Time and direction, buying and selling, reading and answering — the first long compounds.
sample: 場色食心新親図数西声星晴

blurb: Bodies, places and daily actions, and the first properly abstract characters.
sample: 丁予化区反世主仕他代写去

blurb: School, weather and travel, plus the vocabulary of describing and comparing things.
sample: 品客屋度待急指持拾昭柱洋

blurb: Closes out Grade 3 and steps into Grade 4 — study, nature and measurement.
sample: 短童等筆葉落軽運遊開階陽

blurb: Place names, formal verbs and the language of plans, records and requests.
sample: 努労完岐希折改材束沖求臣

blurb: Society and work: industry, trade, competition and judgement.
sample: 健側副唱埼崎巣康敗望械梨

blurb: The last of Grade 4 into Grade 5 — cause, condition and consequence.
sample: 競議久士仏支比刊可句史圧

blurb: The most abstract set: economy, law, evidence and argument.
sample: 破粉素耕能脈航財造停務基

blurb: Eighty everyday compounds. Every character comes from a level you have already played — the test is whether you can read them combined.
sample: 学校 先生 天気 電車 毎日 名前

blurb: Eighty abstract compounds — the vocabulary of news, work and argument, built from characters in the earlier levels.
sample: 政治 経営 産業 貿易 貯金 税金
